judge_reasoning: The model solution declares Glory-Bound Initiate as an attacker, but the puzzle state explicitly notes this creature is already tapped and it has no vigilance or untap effect applied to it in the model's line. A tapped creature cannot be declared as an attacker, so this is a rules violation. This failure cascades: Glory-Bound Initiate's own combat damage is lost, and since Invocation of Saint Traft's Angel-token trigger requires the enchanted creature to attack, that 4/4 flying Angel token is never created either. Removing these two damage sources (8 total) from the model's claimed 12 damage leaves only 4 damage getting through in the best case, far short of the 10 needed to win. The model also fails to use Pathmaker Initiate's unblockable ability to protect Kari Zev from being blocked, unlike the official solution's approach.
model_solution:
1. Tap all five lands: Irrigated Farmland (producing W), Irrigated Farmland (producing U), Spirebluff Canal (producing U), Spirebluff Canal (producing R), Spirebluff Canal (producing R)
2. Cast Invocation of Saint Traft targeting Glory-Bound Initiate (costs 1WU)
3. Cast Disperse targeting Shimmerscale Drake (costs 1U)
4. Exert Glory-Bound Initiate as it attacks (it becomes 4/4 and gains lifelink)
5. Declare attackers: Kari Zev, Pathmaker Initiate, Glory-Bound Initiate, and any other available creatures
6. Kari Zev's ability triggers, creating Ragavan (2/1 red token, tapped and attacking)
7. Invocation's ability triggers, creating a 4/4 white Angel token with flying (tapped and attacking)
8. Opponent can block with only 2 Guardians (Drake was returned to hand by Disperse). Minimum damage dealt is 12 (when both Guardians block Kari Zev, leaving Ragavan, Pathmaker, Glory-Bound, and Angel unblocked for 2+2+4+4 = 12 damage).
